bug_semantics: AuthorizationServerHandler parses the raw JSON body rather than the endpoint DTO and copies every recognized identifier, including an undeclared attacker-added workspaceId and a victim connectionId/sourceId/destinationId, into X-Airbyte-* headers. AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace then trusts X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id before any resource-derived header, so the role check is performed against the attacker's workspace while the endpoint handler operates on the victim resource; no later ownership comparison reconnects the authorization decision to the resource.
flaw_origin: afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d introduced AuthenticationHeaderResolver and wired request headers into Keycloak role lookup. Its initial resolveWorkspace if/else puts WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER ahead of CONNECTION_ID_HEADER, destination, job, source, operation, and config lookups, without checking that simultaneous identifiers resolve to the same workspace. The raw-body header extractor already existed in the parent, so this commit is the smallest repository commit that completed the vulnerable per-workspace authorization mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d` shows human author and committer Xiaohan Song <xiaohan@airbyte.io>; the complete message is `Fetch roles in KeycloakValidator (#8540)` with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-p5mw-j28v-ph9h / CVE-2026-80049 and https://github.com/geo-chen/oss/blob/main/airbyte-platform.md describe the exploitable raw-body workspaceId injection and disclose on 2026-08-25 that upstream had not responded. `git log -L 66,75:airbyte-commons-server/src/main/java/io/airbyte/commons/server/support/AuthenticationHeaderResolver.java afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d` attributes the first WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER-before-CONNECTION_ID_HEADER branch to afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d. Focused `git log -S'properties.containsKey(WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER)'` finds afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d as the first writer; later 8d2a57776d46a764238b4696a075226eca5673ff, a3dbbcd6af6860f475aaaacfd71184577b1a4f0c, and bbf78ce185eab87974a6ed29fcf0928ef83cfac0 are Kotlin migration/revert/migration commits, not origins. Direct parent-tree verification with `git cat-file -e b872bc4729d3ff3dc8f177b997ce7a17a755825a:airbyte-commons-server/src/main/java/io/airbyte/commons/server/support/AuthenticationHeaderResolver.java` fails because the file is absent; the parent's KeycloakTokenValidator grants ADMIN without the new header-based workspace selector. Tag checks show v0.50.26 at 1b263cd817790f91903b66e88f48f5d8d4fe58b0 does not contain the BIC, v0.50.27 at c220f9c4736a1374be017dd8131ae6c7da9c8ec9 does, and v2.0.0 at c46502e96e66083687b15861e05fe8777a9afb59 contains the BIC and both vulnerable Kotlin paths. Commit bda3eed7e67b0bd2ed7a887d16cc3b924389f1cf only strips caller-supplied X-Airbyte headers before repopulating them from the same raw body, so it does not fix workspaceId body injection. Validated clone HEAD 92698410841e010ebd1afafb671fc2fc27398bcc (2026-08-28) still has AuthorizationServerHandler extracting workspaceId from raw JSON and resolveWorkspace prioritizing it; no reachable post-disclosure fix exists.
reasoning: The lifecycle is: the raw request-body extractor and AuthenticationId.WORKSPACE_ID already existed; afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d then created the resolver, made caller-derived workspaceId the first workspace choice, and used that choice to fetch the caller's RBAC role. This completed the confused-deputy path: a valid role in workspace A authorizes an operation whose resource ID belongs to workspace B. The immediate parent has neither the resolver file nor the header-based workspace role decision, proving absence of this flawed mechanism. History searches separate the original Java writer from later mechanical Kotlin migrations, and release ancestry places the BIC between v0.50.26 and v0.50.27 and still in the advisory's v2.0.0 boundary. The repository commit has one parent and no locally/publicly reconstructable PR-member SHAs, so no squash decomposition is claimed. The advisory was unpatched at disclosure and the validated 2026-08-28 HEAD remains vulnerable; therefore both fix fields are null. BIC-only commit-object inspection contains no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched as of validated clone HEAD 92698410841e010ebd1afafb671fc2fc27398bcc on 2026-08-28; no upstream fix SHA or direct-fix SHA exists in the reachable history, and the historical PR #8540 metadata/member commits are no longer publicly reconstructable from the retired repository endpoint.
